name: Student housing
summary: Purpose-built off-campus student housing leased by the bed: 3-5 bedroom units with a bathroom per bedroom, furnished, built as garden, wrap, podium or high-rise near campus. Per-bed cost is driven by the building form (same structure economics as conventional multifamily), bathroom density and furnishing. Public per-bed budgets found are on-campus university projects (Utah 2022, UTEP 2025), which carry dining/student-life space; off-campus figures are therefore derived from the multifamily files and flagged for verification.

typicalSize.method: Typical off-campus PBSH projects of ~150-300 units x 3-4 beds = 400-1,200 beds (judgment); UTEP hall 456 beds (e3), Utah phases 850 and 1,150 beds (e1).

sfPerPrimaryUnit.method: Gross SF per bed: 4BR/4BA units ~1,300-1,450 net SF (~330-360 net SF/bed) at ~80-85% efficiency plus clubhouse/study space => ~420-480 GSF/bed; suburban garden PBSH with larger units at the high end.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Garden PBSH ~20-30 units/acre x 3.5 beds = 70-105 beds/acre; podium/high-rise near campus 200+ beds/acre (derived from garden/podium densities in this category).

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Parking per bed: near-campus podium projects ~0.3-0.5; suburban garden PBSH ~0.8-0.9 (judgment; varies with local code).

perPrimaryUnit.method: Derived: perSF x sfPerPrimaryUnit. Mid $255/GSF (between the garden $185 and podium $290 mids in this category, weighted to mid-rise near-campus product, plus ~3% for a bathroom per bedroom) x 450 GSF/bed ~= $115k/bed. Low ~ garden PBSH $200 x 400 = $80k; high ~ podium/high-rise $340 x 520 = ~$175k. On-campus public projects run higher per bed because they include dining and student-life space: Utah 2022 construction $159,325/bed (e1); UTEP 2025 total project ~$237k/bed incl. soft costs and a dining hall (e3).

perSF.method: Derived from the multifamily product-type ranges (LandSouth garden $130-190 / wrap $200-275 / podium $235-350, e5; RLB 18-city multifamily median $225-410, e4) and this category's garden/podium mids, +~3% for bath-per-bed plumbing and tile.

scope.notes: Contractor price incl. general conditions, OH&P, on-site work, clubhouse/study amenities; excludes land, soft costs, unit furniture (FF&E line), off-sites, impact/tap fees and financing. Podium/high-rise PBSH parking: use the podium/high-rise parking items.

qualityTiers.method: Same tier steps as conventional multifamily (see garden/podium files); luxury reflects high-rise 'amenity-rich' PBSH near flagship campuses.

systemSplit.method: Derived: 50/50 blend of the garden split (RAND-sourced) and podium split (derived) in this category, then +1.5 pts plumbing (22) and +0.5 pts finishes (09) for a bathroom per bedroom, offset by -1.0 pts framing (06) and -1.0 pts site (32); division 01 absorbs rounding.

lineItems.name: Private bathroom per bedroom (fixtures, tile, plumbing rough-in)

cost.method: Derived: compact bathroom (toilet, lav, tub/shower, tile, exhaust, rough-in) ~ $9-18k each (2026 judgment).

lineItems.notes: Carve-out; the defining PBSH cost feature.

cost.method: Derived: 5,000-10,000 SF of amenity space at ~$250-350/SF (2026).

lineItems.name: Bed-level access control and building-wide Wi-Fi

cost.method: Derived: keyless bedroom locks and dense managed Wi-Fi typical of PBSH (2026 judgment).

perPrimaryUnit.method: Derived: furnished bedroom (bed, desk, chair, dresser) plus shared living/dining furniture and amenity FF&E ~ $3,000-6,500 per bed (2026); PBSH is leased furnished.

pctOfHard.method: Utah public project soft/hard 0.20 incl. FF&E and IT (e2, no developer fee); RAND market-rate multifamily 0.19-0.33 incl. financing (e6). Mid 0.23 for a private developer excl. construction interest; FF&E carried separately here.

softCosts.notes: Schedules are tied to August move-in - acceleration premiums and pre-leasing marketing are common soft items.

hard.method: Derived: fixed academic-year delivery date raises schedule risk.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Hard low $80k x 1.15 ~= $92k; hard high $175k x 1.45 ~= $254k; on-campus projects with dining (UTEP ~$237k/bed total, e3) sit near the top.

evidence.region: Salt Lake City, UT (University of Utah)

source.title: New Student Housing - Housing & Residential Education, Board of Higher Education, November 18, 2022 (University of Utah)

evidence.quote: PROJECT BUDGET ... Cost per Bed: Construction $159,325; Soft Costs $31,833 (Design Fees, Permits & Inspection, UIT, FF&E); TOTAL PROJECT $191,208
evidence.scopeNotes: On-campus university housing for ~2,000 beds (Annex 1,150 + Shoreline Ridge 850) including associated dining, retail and student-life space; 2022 budget. On-campus residence halls carry more common/dining area than off-campus purpose-built student housing.

source.title: New Student Housing - Housing & Residential Education, Board of Higher Education, November 18, 2022 (University of Utah)

evidence.quote: Construction $198,467,255 $120,181,215 $159,325 / Soft Costs $ 35,383,307 $ 28,383,641 $ 31,833 (Design Fees, Permits & Inspection, UIT, FF&E)
evidence.scopeNotes: Soft/hard = 31,833 / 159,325 = 0.20 including FF&E and IT; public owner (no developer fee, financing outside budget).

source.title: UT System Regents approve construction of new $108M student housing complex at UTEP (Nov 2025)
source.publisher: The University of Texas at El Paso

evidence.quote: a new $108 million student housing complex ... will house 456 beds ... four-story, co-ed dormitory for freshmen
evidence.scopeNotes: Total project allocation ($108M / 456 beds = ~$237k per bed) for an on-campus freshman residence hall with a large dining hall, fitness and lounges; total project cost incl. soft costs. Not off-campus PBSH.

evidence.region: Median of the 18 US cities in RLB's table

source.title: RLB Construction Cost Report North America Q3 2026 (PDF), Indicative Construction Costs table

evidence.quote: Indicative Construction Costs table, Residential 'Multi-Family' column (US$/SF GFA), 18 US cities from Austin 190-285 to San Francisco 420-700; median LOW 225, median HIGH 410 (computed from the table)
evidence.scopeNotes: RLB: 'Values of U.S. locations represent hard construction costs based on U.S. dollars per square foot of gross floor area.' One 'Multi-Family' column covers all multifamily product (garden to high-rise); sitework treatment not stated. Median of city lows/highs computed by the researcher; the 18 cities skew to large, higher-cost metros.

source.title: Which multifamily product type is right for your site

evidence.quote: Garden-style ... $130 to $190 per square foot; Wrap ... $200 to $275; Podium ... $235 to $350 per square foot
evidence.scopeNotes: Multifamily product-type ranges used as proxies for off-campus student housing built in the same forms.

source.title: The High Cost of Producing Multifamily Housing in California (RAND RR-A3743-1, Ward & Schlake, 2025) - copy hosted by San Diego Housing Commission

evidence.quote: Table 3.1 Panel C. Soft Costs: Texas Market rate $22; Colorado Market rate $44; California Market rate $84 (vs Panel A hard costs $115 / $237 / $253 per NRSF)
evidence.scopeNotes: Soft/hard ratios derived: TX 0.19, CO 0.19, CA 0.33. RAND soft costs include A&E, legal, fees and financing costs; market-rate sample mixes garden, podium, wrap, high-rise.

openQuestions: Off-campus PBSH per-bed hard costs (public REIT disclosures, city incentive applications or university P3 ground-lease budgets) were not found in this pass - the per-bed mid is derived.
Beds per unit and GSF per bed vary widely by market; a sample of recent PBSH projects would tighten sizing.
